thomas-d-allison.text: "Preserving our character does not mean opposing every change. It means ensuring that growth respects the community"; new development should fit neighborhoods, address traffic and parking, and "pay its fair share of the costs it creates."

source.title: Preserving La Verne's Character - Thomas for La Verne (campaign site)

thomas-d-allison.text: "Every cent taken from a resident is a cent that they could be using to improve their own quality of life"; wants the city to exhaust every revenue opportunity before cuts and "prioritize core services before discretionary expansion."

source.title: Fiscal Responsibility - Thomas for La Verne (campaign site)

thomas-d-allison.text: Proposes a "Neighbors Helping Neighbors" program: an active Neighborhood Watch in every District 1 neighborhood and expanded CERT training, plus a voluntary exterior-camera registry police could draw on after incidents.

source.title: Safer Neighborhoods - Thomas for La Verne (campaign site)

thomas-d-allison.text: Says the A Line and "regional homelessness create new public-safety, humanitarian and service-delivery challenges"; advocates auditing alleys, parks and transit approaches for visibility and adding pedestrian-scale lighting.

source.title: Safer Neighborhoods - Thomas for La Verne (campaign site)

thomas-d-allison.text: Urges discussion of staff compensation, opposing having staff "carry the burden of offsetting the costs of our services" and seeking "equitable compensation" so La Verne retains talent; disagrees with the council's vote to limit committees and commissions.

source.title: Fiscal Responsibility - Thomas for La Verne (campaign site)

thomas-d-allison.text: Would "reduce unnecessary barriers for small businesses" and protect Old Town, and advocates protecting the urban tree canopy.

source.title: Preserving La Verne's Character - Thomas for La Verne (campaign site)

steven-frank-johnson.text: (2022) Wanted a local ballot measure returning La Verne to four districts with an elected mayor: "I believe that having an elected mayor is important, and that we should be able to choose as a resident who that person is."
